title: Surgeons Who Play Video Games Make Fewer Mistakes
description:
In one study of 33 doctors doing keyhole-surgery drills, the ones who had played video games for more than 3 hours a week made 37% fewer errors and were 27% faster. Keyhole surgery means steering long tools through tiny holes while watching a flat screen, which is a lot like gaming.

Honest catch: it's one small study and a correlation, not proof that games cause better surgeons. Rosser et al., Archives of Surgery, 2007.

Sources:
- J. C. Rosser Jr et al., 'The impact of video games on training surgeons in the 21st century', Archives of Surgery 142(2):181-186 (2007). doi:10.1001/archsurg.142.2.181 (PubMed 17309970)

How it's made: original 3D characters and scenes, animated by us. The game on screen is our own design. The voices are AI voices (ElevenLabs).

Counterphysical: gaming science that breaks your intuition.
